title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 17)： Stench Athuleet
summary: Part 17 of NH's ongoing mockery series about fitness YouTuber Jason Blaha, this time attacking his claimed athleticism: no footage of sled drags, farmer walks inside his apartment, abandoned Olympic lifting, low pain tolerance, an alleged inability to swim, and unverified fighting and bouncer claims. A few training points surface: avoiding high reps and volume explains poor muscle, and lifting strength does not carry over to fighting.
claims: Claims Blaha told viewers he was bigger than Arnold Schwarzenegger with a bigger chest and triceps, which NH calls delusional
Says Blaha loaded a bumper 5 lb plate beside two 45s and claimed a three-plate front squat, evidence of fake weights
Bodyweight chin-ups should not look agonising after two reps; visible suffering signals very low pain tolerance
A set of 8 on something like a snatch-grip deadlift is not junk volume; people label high reps junk volume because they are painful
Refusing volume and only doing one-rep maxes starves the muscles; strength may rise but muscle will not grow
GPP like sled drags is very demanding on the heart and lungs
Slow pedalling while playing video games or walking a treadmill at 1 mph for 30 minutes does essentially nothing as cardio
Sleds are a great, versatile tool: drag forwards, backwards or push
A squat is not functional athletic training; to demonstrate athleticism you need to move your body
Farmer walks are genuinely hard, harder than a squat single; Blaha quit after about two weeks carrying around 100 lb per hand
The snatch is one of the most technical movements and requires shoulder mobility
A high-carb diet plus low-intensity cardio is what led Blaha to become obese
NH alleges Blaha cannot swim, citing a pool-party refusal and an old bodybuilding.com forum post
Deadlifting heavy does not give you the grip to unscrew a wheel nut by hand
Bouncers usually need to be physically imposing or highly skilled in martial arts
Lifting does not carry over to fighting; a strong lifter who has never fought will last about 25 seconds in a boxing ring
Michael Phelps' 10k kcal/day is justified by his swimming volume; non-athletes using that as an excuse are deluding themselves
A strength athlete who never competes is not really a strength athlete
Bananas are sugary and not filling, so eating six of them is no proof of a big appetite
